This contract does not choose the corpus and does not read the phrase as fixing one: REQ-002 obliges the corpus actually measured over to be identified in the record with the commit state and size counts that make the identification checkable, so that every recorded bound states its own subject (TBD-004).

ClaimText: - CON-003 — The measured act's boundary and vantage are stated by no accepted source. `PEC-API-002` says orientation reads "shall complete in ≤100 ms at p95" and stops there; it does not say where the timed interval begins or ends, nor from whose vantage completion is observed. The register makes the question unavoidable rather than academic: the read path this deliverable is placed on runs through three separately owned contracts — composition (`DEL-04-01`, an in-process interface by its own REQ-011), serialization (`DEL-08-03`), and transport with token resolution before any operation is served (`DEL-08-01`, by its own REQ-002) — and a duration measured over one segment is a different claim from a duration measured over all three. No accepted source apportions the ≤100 ms among them, and this contract apportions none; apportioning it would allocate budget to deliverables whose contracts explicitly disclaim holding any. REQ-003 therefore obliges the boundary and vantage to be declared with every measurement and prohibits aggregation across them, which makes the ambiguity visible in the recorded bound rather than absorbed into a number. It does not settle which boundary the accepted bound intends, and no reading of that intent may be inferred from this document.

ClaimText: - CON-004 — What "an orientation read" contains at measurement time is conditioned by upstream open records and cannot be closed here. `DEL-04-01`'s own `CON-002` and `CON-004`, quoted in full at CLM-007, record that the applicability test and recency ordering for the newest applicable receipt are undefined and that the shape of an honest return for an unreconciled or unknown loop is unsettled; that contract's `CON-001`, not quoted here, records a third gap of the same class, that three of the six required components resolve to no declared record-tier entity type. The consequence lands on this deliverable with a sharpness it does not have upstream, because a duration is a single number into which a conditioning silently disappears: a p95 measured over returns that stated absences against three components is a different claim from a p95 measured over fully composed returns, and the two would be indistinguishable once reported as "orientation reads complete in N ms at p95". REQ-004 therefore obliges the composition state to travel with every measurement and prohibits aggregation across the two cases. That obligation makes the conditioning visible; it does not settle the upstream questions, which remain open in their own contract and are neither resolved nor narrowed here.

ClaimText: - AX-001 — `OBJ-001` governs this deliverable's reason for existing: orientation for any loop is a sub-second query, not a session-length prose derivation. Every other deliverable mapped to that objective builds the answer; this one is the only place where the claim that the answer arrives fast enough is put to a number. That is why REQ-002 through REQ-005 are stated as obligations on the record rather than as good practice: a latency figure is the most portable and the most easily decontextualized artifact this project will produce, and it will outlive the run that produced it.

ClaimText: - AX-002 — The bound is stated and is therefore carried, not set. `PEC-API-002` fixes ≤100 ms at p95 in the accepted sources, so this contract's discipline runs opposite to the one its `PKG-03` counterpart needs: there is no numeric gap to route to an owner, and the temptation here is the reverse one — to soften a stated number into a target when a measurement is inconvenient, or to tighten it into an implied service-level promise the sources do not make. REQ-001 forbids both directions, and REQ-009 keeps the disposition of a failing measurement a recorded fact rather than a verdict this deliverable issues.

ClaimText: - AX-003 — A measurement conditions its own claim, and the conditioning is the part that disappears first. `PEC-K-08` requires that "Every status, verdict, and warning carries rule ID, threshold, and contributing cited sources. Drill-down never dead-ends", and a p95 with no corpus, no boundary, no sample, and no composition state is precisely a verdict whose drill-down dead-ends. REQ-002 through REQ-005 exist so that each recorded figure carries the four things that determine what it is a figure *about*, and the prohibitions on aggregation exist because averaging across conditions is how a conditioned claim becomes an unconditioned one without anyone deciding that it should.

ClaimText: - AX-004 — Measuring three contracts imposes nothing on any of them. `[E-P51]`, `[E-N12]`, and `[E-P52]` all run *into* this deliverable, and each predecessor's own contract already records this one as the measurer and disclaims the budget in its own voice (CLM-007, CLM-008, CLM-009). CON-003 and CON-004 record gaps in the upstream record and assign work in neither place: a measurement that started specifying how a return should be composed, what an envelope should contain, or how a token should be issued would have left this deliverable's scope in exactly the way the `PKG-10` instrument contract warns against for its own case.

ClaimText: - AX-005 — A stand-in is not the thing. The measured path does not exist, and the honest form of that fact is not to wait but to time a stand-in and say so. REQ-006 permits the stand-in and forbids the elision, because the failure mode is silent and one-directional: a stand-in number recorded without its label is indistinguishable from a real-surface measurement six months later, and it will be quoted as one. The same reasoning is why the stand-in inventory belongs in the budget record rather than in a test comment.

ClaimText: - AX-006 — Adjacency on a path is not an allocation of the budget. The serializer sits on the measured path and the socket carries it, and neither fact makes any part of the ≤100 ms theirs to hold or this contract's to assign. `DEL-08-03`'s own `CON-001` records that "compact" has no accepted metric and names this deliverable's budget as the nearest one in the corpus; supplying that metric from here — by apportioning milliseconds, or by declaring what a compact response costs — would answer an upstream open question with a number this contract has no source for. This deliverable owns the budget; it does not own, and does not define, the properties of the things that spend it.

ClaimText: - AX-007 — `PEC-K-10` content-minimal governs what a measurement may retain. A latency harness reads a corpus of governed prose and has every incentive to keep payloads around for debugging, which is the one place file content could enter through a deliverable whose outputs are numbers. REQ-011 binds the capture side directly rather than relying on the ingest guard, because the suite's retention is outside any path that guard covers.

ClaimText: - AX-008 — Read-only means the measured corpus is unchanged by having been measured. `PEC-K-06` observation-not-participation and the graceful-absence posture make PEC's own state deletable; a performance suite that mutated the corpus to make a run reproducible would corrupt the subject of every subsequent measurement and would do so invisibly, since the artifact of the corruption is a faster number. REQ-010 states the boundary as a checkable property with a before-and-after hash rather than as a discipline.

ClaimText: - AX-009 — The DECLARED sequencing edge is respected as sequencing and nothing more. `[E-A28]` records that the Step-0 baseline is measured before `P1` begins and that it *baselines* `SOW-041`; it does not make that baseline an input this suite reads, a comparator for its figures, or a source of its bound, and the upstream contract states in its own voice that what is measured before `P1` is the cost of the prose derivation, "not the cost of any PEC capability, which does not yet exist at `pre-P1`". Token cost and wall-clock latency are different metrics over different subjects. Reading a `DECLARED` stratum as a stronger claim on this contract's content than its own text supports would be the same error in the opposite direction from ignoring it.

ClaimText: - AX-010 — Stratum is provenance, not authority. `C-10` `STRATUM_RULE` ends "All strata require owner acceptance; strata are provenance not authority", and this deliverable's upstream set spans two strata, so the distinction is load-bearing here rather than decorative. `D-PEC-62` §1(4) accepts all four edges — "accepted, all strata as presented" — and that packet reads "as presented" as taking the exhibit's flags as flags, leaving a specific annotated set recorded-but-unresolved and non-gating; none of the annotations it names is an edge cited in this contract, and every edge cited here carries an empty `Flag` cell. Provenance is not authority in either direction: the `DECLARED` edge is not thereby a stronger obligation on content, and the three `PROPOSAL` edges are not thereby weaker ones. The one annotation from that set this contract touches at all is the `C-08` standing-node question, cited at CLM-005 and CON-006 precisely as unresolved.

ClaimText: - AX-012 — Unknowns stay marked. TBD-001 through TBD-004 and CON-001 through CON-006 are recorded rather than resolved by authoring judgment. Three of the six conflicts are wholly or partly upstream-carried — the surfaces that do not exist, the content of a return, and the properties of what rides the path — and settling any of them here would take a determination in the wrong place while making it look like a measurement detail.
